title: "cEOS Interfaces and LLDP"

# cEOS Interfaces and LLDP

Before VLANs, learn the port names. Containerlab's `eth1` is EOS `Ethernet1`. LLDP is how you prove the cable you think you built is the cable the switch sees.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Map `eth` names to EOS and SR Linux names
- Read LLDP neighbours on cEOS and SR Linux
- Tell a management port from a data port
- Explain why an interface can be up in Linux and down in the NOS

## Topology

Two nodes and one link are enough. Reuse the kind block from the lab host chapter.

```yaml
name: lldp
topology:
  kinds:
    arista_ceos:
      image: ceos:4.37.0F
      memory: 2G
    nokia_srlinux:
      image: ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux:latest
      memory: 2G
  nodes:
    sw:
      kind: arista_ceos
    srl:
      kind: nokia_srlinux
  links:
    - endpoints: ["sw:eth1", "srl:ethernet-1/1"]
```

## Config

cEOS, after `Cli` answers:

```text
interface Ethernet1
   description to-srl
   no shutdown
lldp run
```

SR Linux:

```text
enter candidate
set system lldp admin-state enable
set interface ethernet-1/1 admin-state enable
set interface ethernet-1/1 description to-ceos
commit now
```

Leave the port as a switchport on cEOS. LLDP does not need an IP address.

## Verify

```bash
docker exec clab-lldp-sw Cli -c "show lldp neighbors"
docker exec clab-lldp-sw Cli -c "show interfaces Ethernet1 status"
docker exec clab-lldp-srl sr_cli "show system lldp neighbor"
containerlab inspect interfaces -t topology.clab.yml
```

### Predict

- `show lldp neighbors` on cEOS names the SR Linux chassis on Ethernet1.
- Ethernet1 is connected. Management0 has the Docker address and is not in the LLDP table for this link.
- `show interfaces Ethernet2` is down. Nothing is cabled there.

## Drill

Add a second link, `sw:eth2` to `srl:ethernet-1/2`, deploy with `--reconfigure` only if you destroyed the lab first, and confirm LLDP shows two neighbours. Then shut Ethernet2 and watch that neighbour disappear within one LLDP hold time.
